g.text: Term
Term
Description
Description
asset
item, thing or entity that has potential or actual value to an organization. {{cite
> Note 1 to entry: Value can be tangible or intangible, financial or non-
financial, and includes consideration of risks and liabilities. It can be positive
or negative at different stages of the asset life.
> Note 2 to entry: Physical assets usually refer to equipment, inventory and
properties owned by the organization. Physical assets are the opposite of
intangible assets, which are non-physical assets such as leases, brands,
digital assets, use rights, licences, intellectual property rights, reputation or
agreements.
> Note 3 to entry: A grouping of assets referred to as an asset system could
also be considered as an asset.
condition
ability of a piece of equipment or {{term(Component)}} to function to
specification.
condition state
indicator of the {{term(condition)}}.
configuration
information about an {{term(engineered system)}} describing its physical
layout, functional characteristics, and relationships with other {{termplural
(engineered system)}}
control limit
limit used to indicate whether a process variable is stable and in control.
engineered system
logical or physical entity that may produce {{termplural(observation)}} about
itself.
engineering units
quantity, dimension, or magnitude used in engineering adopted as a
standard in terms of which the magnitude of other quantities of the same
kind can be expressed or calculated.
equipment
represents anything that can publish information and is used in the
operations of a manufacturing facility shop floor.
> Note: Examples include machine tools, ovens, sensor units, workstations,
software applications, and bar feeders.
equipment metadata
{{term(metadata)}} that defines both the entities that represent the physical
and logical parts and sub-parts of each piece of equipment, the
relationships between those parts and sub-parts, and the definitions of the
{{termplural(DataItem)}} associated with that piece of equipment.
observable
quality, property, or characteristic that can be observed.
observation
observed value of a property at a point in time.
observe
act of measuring or determining the value of a property at a point in time.
physical connection
network transmission technologies that physically interconnect an {{term
(agent)}}.
raw material
crude or processed material that can be converted by manufacture,
processing, or combination into a new and useful product.
resource
physical or logical entity used by an organization
sensor
{{term(sensing element)}} that responds to a physical stimulus and transmits
a resulting signal.
sensor configuration
data in the {{term(MTConnectDevices Response Document)}} that provides
the information required for maintenance and support of the {{term(sensor
unit)}}.
sensor data
value of a physical quantity reported by a measuring instrument or controller
as an {{term(observation)}}.
sensor element
provides a signal or measured value.
sensor unit
intelligent piece of equipment that manages the signals of one or more
{{termplural(sensing element)}} and provides the measured values.
Thing
property holder.
> Note 1 to entry: Property holders are used to define properties that have
no specific owner, or “top level” properties. These properties are generally
referenced by other properties. {{cite(https://www.omg.org/spec/NIEM-
> Note 2 to entry: Property holder is equivalent to one topmost class of
which all other classes are subclasses.
